chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Any man who frightens a man while he is on a wall, or causes his mount to shy away with him so that he falls and dies, then he is liable for his blood money. And if he is injured with a fracture, then he is liable for the compensation of whatever is fractured of him.

key_terms.الْجِدَارِ: a wall or elevated structure from which one may fall
key_terms.انْكَسَرَ: suffered a fracture or broken limb
key_terms.دِيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or death
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.لِدِيَتِهِ: for his blood money compensation in case of death

ai.seo_question: Is a person legally liable if they frighten someone and cause them to fall, die, or suffer a fracture?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes legal liability for causing harm through frightening or startling someone in a dangerous situation. If such an act leads to death, the perpetrator is responsible for the diyah, and if it causes bodily fracture, he is responsible for the corresponding compensation.
